newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's CIADEA says Renault may take control.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's CIADEA says Renault may take control.

text.p: Argentine carmaker CIADEA SA, licensee of France's Renault, said Thursday Renault plans to take control of the holding company that in turn controls CIADEA.

Renault "has expressed that it intends to take control of the trade-mark activity in Argentina," Omar Daneri, a CIADEA vice-president, told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter. He not say how CIADEA came by the information.

"Renault plans to concentrate in a single company the whole of its industrial interests in Mercosur," he added, referring to the regional customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

Daneri said Renault may bring into Compagnie Financiere pour l'Amerique Latine (COFAL), the holding company that controls CIADEA, the 60 percent stake it has in Renault do Brasil Automoveis. As a consequence, Renault would end up being the main shareholder of COFAL, Daneri said.
He added that, in Argentina, COFAL would keep its current 51 percent stake in CIADEA and Renault wants Manuel Antelo to remain president of CIADEA.
But Daneri said CIADEA was not aware any agreement had yet been signed to put into effect the above changes.
